title: Leaving a Plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans at the Retiree's Own Election
content:
Only the retiree may choose to leave a group plan of their own accord, and the plan never records a voluntary disenrollment on a sponsor's word. That holds on every plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans alike.

## The condition on recording a voluntary disenrollment

The disenrollment comes from the retiree themselves, recorded as a change of type retiree-requested disenrollment sourced from the retiree.

The source of the change is read from the plan's own change records, before the disenrollment is recorded, and on the change record itself. The retiree's own request is the only source that answers the condition; a change carried by the sponsor's eligibility file or by a written sponsor instruction does not.

## The day cover ends

A voluntary disenrollment takes effect on the last day of the month the request was received, and the retiree keeps full cover until that day.

## Rejoining, and drug coverage afterwards

A retiree who leaves a group plan ordinarily cannot rejoin it until the sponsor's next open enrollment, and the plan says which month that is before the request is recorded.

A retiree leaving a group plan that includes drug coverage is told they must arrange other creditable drug coverage or face a late enrollment penalty later.

## Declining the plan before it takes effect

A retiree declining the plan before it ever takes effect leaves no coverage period and owes no contribution at all.

## After the retiree's death

A surviving spouse may stay on the group plan for the continuation months scheduled for that plan after the retiree's death, and is told the date their own cover would end.
